text:
From being completely reliant on imports for energy, to becoming a major player in the market, Nigeria has turned its fortunes around by pivoting to an exporter of fuel, courtesy of the Dangote Refinery, the world’s largest single-train refinery.
Tankers lifting refined petrol from the Dangote refinery Nigeria has transformed from a fuel importer to a major fuel exporter, driven by the Dangote Refinery. For the first time in decades, Nigeria became a net fuel exporter in April, supplying about 44,000 barrels per day. Petroleum products now comprise 53.5% of British imports from Nigeria, with purchases more than doubling in a year. The Dangote Refinery's turnaround saw it earn $4.725 billion and reach $22.5 billion in revenue after last year’s loss. The first time Nigeria’s relevance in the global energy economy was highlighted was when the West African country was reported to have become a net exporter of fuel.
In April this year, it was reported that Nigeria had become a net exporter of fuel for the first time in decades, marking a turning point for a country long defined by its dependence on imported fuel despite being Africa’s largest oil producer .
At the time, data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that Nigeria exported about 44,000 barrels per day (bpd) of petrol, slightly exceeding imports and leaving a net surplus of roughly 3,000 bpd.
Currently, Nigeria’s foray into the global fuel supply has made headlines, with reports of fuel supply to the UK amounting to £1.02 billion.

The data also reveal a sharp increase in purchases, with British imports of refined oil from Nigeria more than doubling over the 12 months to June 2026 compared with the previous year's corresponding period.
This pushed petroleum products ahead of other Nigerian exports to become the UK's largest import category, as seen in the Punch newspaper.
This growth coincides with Dangote’s expansion plans, which would see the establishment of a new oil refinery in East Africa, as well as the expansion of the refining capacity at his refinery in Lagos.
Additionally, the move follows the remarkable revenue growth the Dangote Refinery recorded this year after last year’s loss.
The $20 billion refinery swung back to profitability, posting earnings of $4.725 billion after recording a loss during the same period last year.
Its revenue also climbed to $22.5 billion, more than twice the previous year's figure, as the facility ramped up operations to process as much as 700,000 barrels of crude oil daily.
The company also reported a cash balance of $650.8 million, a significant shift from the $1.7 billion in debt it recorded a year earlier.
